description:
You wake up. The street is silent. Then the groaning starts, and your dad wants to bring the leaf blower.
A very serious radio, a dad in shorts and one dog with a ham try to survive a Saturday morning on Maple Street.

lines.text: Part one. You wake up. It is Saturday. The street is silent.
Why is the radio talking to me like I'm the main character?
Because you are the main character. Sit up slowly.
I am sitting up slowly because it's six in the morning.
Then, outside, you hear it. The groaning.
Nora! Nobody panic! I am already panicking for all of us!
Dad, why are you wearing shorts in November?
No time for questions. The neighbors are moving very slowly.
The neighbors always move slowly. They're the neighbors.
Not like this. Mister Delgado is walking with both arms out.
He does that when he carries the mail. Good morning, by the way.
Pudding? You can talk?
Only in emergencies. And at dinner. Dinner is also an emergency.
You have two choices. The front door, or the kitchen window.
Kitchen window. Nobody expects a window.
Dad, the kitchen window is the size of a toaster.
Then we will be very small and very fast.
You chose the window. You do not fit. Part one is over.
Part two. Supplies. Pack only what you need to survive.
Okay. Leaf blower.
Why a leaf blower?
If they get close, I blow them back. Gently. Like leaves.
They're people, Dad. They are not leaves.
Everybody is a leaf if the blower is big enough.
I am packing the ham.
We don't need a whole ham.
You don't. I do. I have a plan, and the plan is ham.
Pack a flashlight. Pack water. Do not pack the ham.
Too late. The ham is already packed. Inside me.
The flashlight is dead. It has been dead since the Fourth of July.
Why do we keep a dead flashlight?
Emotional support.
You have one working light. It is me. I am also the radio. I do a lot.
Your battery says eleven percent.
Then listen carefully. And quickly.
Part three. You step outside. The air is cold. Something shuffles past the mailbox.
Get down! Behind the recycling!
Dad, the recycling bin is see-through.
Then think solid thoughts.
That is Mrs. Kowalski. She is groaning.
She's holding her knees. And an empty water bottle.
That's how it starts. First the knees. Then the water bottle.
She sees you. She raises one arm. She says one word.
Here it comes.
Water.
Okay, that is not a zombie word. That is a thirsty word.
Zombies get thirsty. It's in all the movies I fell asleep during.
More of them appear. They are all wearing matching shirts.
Matching shirts? Dad, zombies don't coordinate.
These ones are organized. That's what makes them so dangerous.
Mister Delgado has a number on his shirt. Forty two.
He's been counting victims!
He can't count to forty two. I watched him pay for a pizza.
You must choose. Run to the garage, or hide inside the inflatable snowman.
The snowman. Nobody looks inside a snowman.
Because there's nothing inside a snowman, Dad. It's air.
Then we will become the air.
You chose the snowman. The fan is very loud. Your hair now points straight up.
I have never looked better in my life.
Can we please just pick the garage next time?
Part four. The garage. You barricade the door with lawn chairs.
Four lawn chairs. The cooler. And the good rake.
You're protecting the good rake from zombies?
I protect the good rake from everybody. Your uncle borrowed it in two thousand twelve.
There is knocking.
Knock. Knock. Knock. Then a voice. It says, Hal.
They know my name! They've learned names!
Your name is on the mailbox in giant gold letters.
That was for style.
The voice says, Hal, you have the water.
Lies. Zombie lies. I have a leaf blower and a ham.
You do not have a ham. I have the ham.
Leaf blower, engage!
You pull the cord. It does not start. You pull it again. It does not start.
Dad. It's electric. It's not plugged in.
So I've been pulling a decorative cord.
You plug it in. It blows every leaf you raked yesterday back into the garage.
This is the best morning of my whole life.
We raked for four hours!
And now the leaves are home. Safe. With family.
Part five. There is a sign taped to the garage door. You read it.
Maple Street Fall Fun Run. Starts at five thirty. Water station at Hal's garage.
Oh.
Dad.
Oh, no.
Are the zombies just our neighbors running a fun run?
They are not zombies. They are runners. This is mile two. They have waited for water for forty minutes.
In my defense, I organized it.
That is not a defense! That makes it so much worse!
I made the shirts. I made the sign. I put the route past our house so I could sleep in.
And you did sleep in. You were very good at it.
So you're wearing shorts because you're running the whole thing.
I'm wearing shorts because I'm number one. Look.
You look. His shirt says number one. Underneath, it says water guy.
Water guy, Dad. You had one job and it was printed on your body.
I thought the water guy was a different guy!
There is no different guy. There is never a different guy.
You open the door. Twenty neighbors look at you. Slowly. With love, and anger.
Good morning, Maple Street! Who wants a cold water and a warm ham?
Not the ham.
Mrs. Kowalski is drinking straight from the hose.
Hydration is hydration.
Mister Delgado finishes his water. He says, best fun run ever. The leaf blower at mile two was a nice touch.
See? Leaf blower. Big hit.
You blew leaves into a man's face and he said thank you.
That's community.
Battery at two percent. Part six, tomorrow. The cooldown.
Wait. There's a cooldown?
Dad. You organized it.
Then who is running the cooldown?
Me. I am running the cooldown. With the ham.
